This "game", software, aim trainer, whatever it can be cailed... It's horrible. 

Aim Labs is one of the messiest, ugliest "games" I have ever had the luxury of using. I have only played for about 15 minutes, made an account, got my tier and tested a few modes for fun, and was absolutely shocked by how unpleasant and horrible this played.

For 20 GB, you would sure hope that this would be worth using at all. In 20 GB i could download Grand Theft Auto 4, an early Call of Duty title, the legacy version of Counter Strike: Global Offensive, and a load of other games that could *actually* give me some aiming practice, as well as proper multiplayer. Instead, I was not allowed to paste my password in when making an account, making my password manager essentially useless, so I opted for a more... throwaway password.

And I think this was one of the worst things I've ever touched. Charging money every month for an aim trainer, much less one that is supposedly "free", is insane. The way this game is moderated in general has a lot of issues, from allowing you to pay for weapon skins to the ability for the target to flash red when "shot". You know, a feature that is an essential GIVEN in any title you can play nowadays? Would you like me to also pay for every 10 minutes of gameplay?

For the money you spend on an aim trainer like this (every month, no less), you could just as easily buy a skin in whatever game you're training for (be it Counter-Strike or Valorant, or anything in between) and a bit of their virtual currency. Why you would also want to pay for cosmetics on an aim trainer that you won't be revisiting for fun frequently is insanity.

You can argue that other aim trainers cost money, so this one is automatically better for being free. Except it's not, because they charge all the cool and NORMALLY GIVEN ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ under a subscription.

You would think if they are charging a subscription, the game would at least be good, or at least look nice. Except it doe…
You have to pay for a monthly subscription to really utilize this.

lmao do not get this. its free but you have to pay a MONTHLY SUBSCRIPTION for any features other than shooting at a target. theres literally no reason not to just practice in the game youre trying to be good at

if you want to get those features, you have to create an account and collect an assload of data on you:

your scores, account info, and possibly gameplay recordings, plus mouse movement and keystroke patterns, which they legally count as "biometric data." your performance stats can be public on leaderboards unless you turn on anonymous mode, and linking accounts pulls in even more data.

they say they don't "sell" your info, but sharing it with advertisers might count and opting out is on you, not automatic. They also share data with a bunch of third parties (ad networks, analytics/session-recording tools), don't honor "Do Not Track," and don't cap how long they keep your data.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface has become cluttered and bloated over time, making it difficult to find previously used features and menus.

citations.review_text: Every change made in the last 5 years should be reversed they bloated this thing to the point I can't find anything. Thank god I made some custom playlists back in 2019 before they nuked this app. Legit feels like they tried to be the roblox of aim trainers.

When they started out this was a great program to test and train your aim. As time does though it moves forward and sometimes we get it wrong. This game/app/training software aged like unpasteurized milk. It's bloated and over barren. Then everything you used to use got buried in the clutter. No way to adjust the menu's to get to the things you use to use daily without digging past everything new they want to show you.

Content creators and 'pro' player embeds everywhere. As a marketing strategy? I don't care about either.

Then there's the whole people testing aimbots against tasks. You can look at the leaderboards and visit the replays. Watch as someone flicks in perfect straight lines and when a mistake is made it's corrected the same as any other mistake. Leaderboards flooded with cheats weekly, monthly, and yearly. If you know what you're looking at.
Even the best angle snapping mouse still allows for a bit of a curve now and then. 

With them not cleaning up leaderboards or banning these people leaderboards have no value. The other side of the coin is the people doing this aren't really there for just the leaderboard. Their testing humanized aiming and training it to look legitimate. They do the best scores but realistically only for a laugh. Then they tune it more and more like the best aimers known. So they'll be less likely to be banned by a program when they play another game. This program without anti cheat is less a tool for improving your aim and more a tool for humanizing your aimbot.

It became less and less appealing with every update. Instead of being a straightforward training tool, it's turned into something with Clash Royale level monetization. If you can tolerate a terrible UI, unnecessary bloat, and awful QoL in the hope that it'll eventually improve, you might find some use in it. Otherwise, just get Kovaak's or use Human Benchmark instead.
